title: Identifier cannot be modified after item creation
gherkin:
Feature: Identifier Immutability
  Scenario: Prevent modification of item identifier after creation
    Given an item has been created with identifier "ITEM-12345"
    When an authorized user attempts to modify the item identifier to "ITEM-67890"
    Then the system shall reject the modification
    And the item identifier shall remain "ITEM-12345"
    And an error message shall indicate that identifier modification is not permitted
rationale: The identifier immutability rule requires that once an identifier is assigned during item creation, it cannot be changed. This is critical for maintaining referential integrity, especially in warehouse operations where identifiers are used for scanning and tracking. Evidence shows concerns about identifier consistency across operational and business-facing contexts, making immutability essential to prevent data divergence.
usedContextItems: Identifier immutability rule|Preserve identifier consistency for downstream operational processes|Stable identifier strategy

Subject: Review findings on reporting consistency

Hi Dev Team,

During our recent reporting review, we found several consistency issues that need clarification before the reporting package can be considered reliable for audit use.

First, the financial outputs do not appear to align cleanly across all billing contexts. In some cases, the figures shown in reports, exported files, and billing records seem to reflect different presentation or calculation assumptions.

Second, the activity and audit views currently favor a privacy-preserving identifier style that makes operational review harder for non-technical auditors. Third, exported reporting artifacts do not always appear to match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform, which raises a broader question about which data representation should be treated as authoritative for audit purposes.

Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Gary (Logistics)

Feature: Audit Trail for Identifier Protection
  Scenario: System logs all attempts to modify identifiers
    Given an item with identifier "AUDIT-001"
    When a user attempts to modify the identifier
    Then the system shall reject the modification
    And an audit log entry shall be created recording:
      | Field | Value |
      | Event Type | Identifier Modification Attempt |
      | Item Identifier | AUDIT-001 |
      | Attempted New Value | <attempted_value> |
      | User ID | <user_id> |
      | Timestamp | <current_timestamp> |
      | Result | Rejected |
    And the audit log shall be immutable and tamper-evident
rationale: Comprehensive audit logging of identifier modification attempts is essential for compliance and security. This test ensures that the system maintains a complete record of any attempts to violate the immutability rule, supporting both operational oversight and regulatory compliance requirements mentioned in the evidence.

Subject: Review findings on reporting consistency

Hi Dev Team,

During our recent reporting review, we found several consistency issues that need clarification before the reporting package can be considered reliable for audit use.

First, the financial outputs do not appear to align cleanly across all billing contexts. In some cases, the figures shown in reports, exported files, and billing records seem to reflect different presentation or calculation assumptions.

Second, the activity and audit views currently favor a privacy-preserving identifier style that makes operational review harder for non-technical auditors. Third, exported reporting artifacts do not always appear to match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform, which raises a broader question about which data representation should be treated as authoritative for audit purposes.

Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Gary (Logistics)
